events.motion: This House believes that the Constitution should not regulate Hindu temples
events.description:
HIPL launches with an evening in the company of scholars, jurists, writers, thinkers and young voices, and with its first Dialogue: a formal debate on who should run Hindu temples.

The room votes on the motion before the debate and again after it. We announce the shift, not a winner.
events.brief:
Many major Hindu temples in India are managed under state laws, through boards and departments that oversee their administration and finances. Supporters say this protects devotees, prevents mismanagement and keeps temples open to all. Critics say it singles out Hindu institutions, takes decisions about worship away from communities, and diverts temple funds.

The motion asks whether the Constitution should allow the state to regulate Hindu temples at all. Speakers will argue both sides; the full background reading list will be posted here before the evening.
